name: Updating Two-Dimensional Array (Case 1)
description: Construct a program that initializes a 3x4 two-dimensional matrix that has the numbers 1 through 12 for entries, sets the left-most element in the middle row of the matrix to be 20, and finally prints all the elements in the matrix.

comments.content: We need to use two-dimensional array (an array of arrays) to create a matrix. Each matrix row corresponds to a subarray in the two-dimensional array. This statement creates a 3x4 two-dimensional array called matrix and initializes its entries with numbers 1 through 12.
Note that arrays can naturally span multiple lines if we want them to because they are contained by braces.
This statement sets the left-most element in the middle row of the matrix to be 20.

In a two-dimensional array, we can access an element within a matrix row (a nested subarray) by using two indices. The first index in [] is the row index and the second index in [] is the column index. The row index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the two-dimensional array, i.e., the number of rows in the two-dimensional array. The column index could start at 0 and continue up to but not including the length of the row, i.e., the number of elements within the row.

The left-most element of a row has the column index of 0. We want to update the element in the middle row of the matrix, so we should use the row index of 1. So, matrix[1][0] corresponds to the left-most element in the middle row of the matrix.

To access each element of a two dimensional array, we need to iterate through the matrix indexes using two for loops. We need two for loops because we need two indexes to access an individual element from a 2D array. The outer for loop iterates through the rows in the matrix and the inner for loop iterates through the columns in the matrix.

This statement is the outer for loop that iterates through the matrix rows.

We need the row indexes to start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every integer number up to but not including the number of rows in the matrix.
matrix.length gives us the number of rows in the matrix.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable i and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less matrix.length and terminates when the control variable reaches matrix.length. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable i and the result is stored back into the variable i. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement i = i + 1.
This statement is the inner for loop that iterates through the matrix columns in the row i.

We need the column indexes to start at 0 (array indexes start from 0) with every integer number up to but not including the number of columns in the matrix.
matrix[0].length gives us the number of columns in the matrix.

In the first part of the loop header, we define a control variable j and initialize it to 0. In the second part of the loop header, we test whether the control variable has reached the termination threshold. The loop is repeated if the control variable is less matrix[0].length and terminates when the control variable reaches matrix[0].length. In the third part of the loop header, we increment the control variable by 1 after each iteration of the loop.
Note that the first part is executed once before the loop starts, the second part is executed before each iteration, and the third part is executed after each iteration of the loop.
Also note that the increment operator (++) adds 1 to the value of variable j and the result is stored back into the variable j. Therefore, it is functionally equivalent to the statement j = j + 1.
This statement prints the element at the row i and column j of the matrix followed by a space character.

Note that we don't use println because it adds an end-of-line character to terminate the output line. We want to print all the elements in the row i in the same line; therefore, we use the print method.
When all elements in the row i are printed, this statement gets executed and prints a new line to the default standard output stream.
